title: triticum turgidum subsp. maroccanum
intro: Triticum turgidum subsp. maroccanum, commonly known as durum wheat, is a subspecies of durum wheat, a type of wheat that is widely cultivated for its grain and is often used in the production of pasta and bread. This plant is rich in nutrients and has been associated with various health benefits, including reducing inflammation, improving cardiovascular health, and aiding in digestion. The therapeutic actions of durum wheat include antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties, which contribute to its potential health benefits. The bioactive constituents of durum wheat include phenolic compounds, such as ferulic acid, caffeic acid, and p-coumaric acid, which are responsible for its therapeutic actions.
